scope: Theorem 10.4 (Charged expected running time) of the manuscript “An Almost-Linear Approximation Scheme for Edit Distance” (preprints/An-Almost-Linear-Approximation-Scheme-for-Edit-Distance-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 121 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 7ecda63faaa7d6a3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 43. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The large-input algorithm has worst-case expected running time N1+o(1) on the logarithmic-word RAM, over its internal randomness. This includes input processing, preprocessing, initial and refined table calculations, all rational arithmetic, sampling, and data-structure operations. Its workspace on every execution is bounded by a fixed polynomial in N. Together with the exact fallbacks, the same program has the claimed expected asymptotic bound for each fixed rational ε ∈ (0, 1).
